outcomes.text: Respond to oral prompts related to classroom behaviors (e.g., Raise your hand; Open your book) with gestures.
Follow instructions related to classroom behaviors (e.g. sharing; turn taking) through role play.
Identify positive ways of interacting socially based on oral descriptions with a partner.
Compare positive and negative solutions to peer pressure based on oral descriptions during teacher facilitated discussion.
Make connections to self from oral scenarios involving peer interactions.
Select illustrations representing main ideas based on simple oral words/phrases using a word bank.
Select illustrations representing main ideas based on brief oral descriptive phrases using a word bank.
Identify main idea and supporting detail based on oral descriptions using sentence frames.
Connect main idea and supporting details based on a teacherread passage with a partner using graphic organizer.
Summarize main ideas and supporting details based on teacher-read fiction/nonfiction during small groups.
Match twodimensional shapes three-dimensional shapes and twodimensional shapes from an oral description with a partner using single words or phrases.
Select twodimensional shapes three-dimensional shapes and twodimensional shapes from an oral description with a partner reading brief descriptions.
Select twodimensional shapes three-dimensional shapes and twodimensional shapes from an oral description with a partner reading a paragraph
Match two dimensional shapes three-dimensional shapes and twodimensional shapes from an oral description with a partner using grade level specific vocabulary (e.g., polygon, cube, tetrahedral).
Select two dimensional shapes three-dimensional shapes and twodimensional shapes after an oral description from a presentation to the whole class.
Critique peer science fair presentations with a rubric and an interpreter.
Critique peer science fair presentations with a rubric with icons (e.g., Likert Scale) and a partner.
Critique peer science fair presentations with a rubric with icons (e.g., Likert Scale).
Critique peer science fair presentations with a rubric and a partner.
Critique peer science fair presentations with a rubric.
Locate places or geographic features on a map from oral description..
Select appropriate maps to identify regions, countries or landforms from oral description.
Select appropriate maps based on oral descriptions about regions, countries, landforms or manmade structures.
Compare and contrast different types of maps from oral descriptions using a graphic organizer.
Construct a representation of different types of maps from oral descriptions.
Arrange pictures and symbols with words and phrases in everyday print (e.g., menu, signs, newspaper) in L1 or L2.
Find key information from everyday print (e.g., menu, signs, newspaper) with visual supports.
Categorize relevant and irrelevant information on topics gathered from everyday print on a tchart with a partner.
Draw conclusions on topics gathered from everyday print in highlighted text.
Summarize information on topics gathered from everyday print while independently reading.
Match words to illustrations that reflect main ideas of an illustrated text.
Locate phrases that reflect the main ideas of an illustrated text.
Analyze the use of illustrations, headings, captions, vocabulary to determine the central idea of a text with a partner.
Identify the central and related ideas of a text in sentences using a story map while working in a small group.
Select and explain the best summary of the central and related ideas of a text in a group of three to four.
Match order of operations terms with symbols with teacher prompting.
Identify key terms to determine the order of operations in a shared reading of a story problem.
Demonstrate the order of multi-step problems using manipulatives.
Follow written directions to solve a multi-step problem based on models.
Solve a multi-step problem working with a partner.
Match names of recyclable objects with Illustrations with a bilingual dictionary.
Match sentence strips to illustrations of the steps in the recycling process with a partner.
Identify the steps and outcomes of a community recycling program in a highlighted or chunked newspaper article.
Summarize the benefits of a community recycling program in a newspaper article using a graphic organizer.
Predict outcomes of a community recycling program in a newspaper article using class notes.
Identify words and phrases from text and charts with visual support.
Classify data based on information from text and charts using a graphic organizer.
Compare data based on information from text and charts using a graphic organizer.
Analyze data based on information and charts in a small group.
Predict future trends based on data gleaned from grade-level text and charts in a small group.
State greetings, compliments, introductions, or farewells in authentic context using one or two words while roleplaying.
Ask and respond to simple WHconversational questions or exchange information with picture cues.
Exchange everyday information using conversation models with partners.
Participate in conversation using idiomatic expressions or slang in a small group.
Participate in conversation using idiomatic expressions of slang with a partner.
Repeat key vocabulary (WH-words) that demonstrate main ideas using illustrated flash cards.
Describe the main idea using short phrases with a partner.
Connect three details to one main idea with an adapted text in a small group of 3-4.
Explain the connection between different details and at least two main ideas in a small group of 3-4.
Debate the main idea and cite details with self-selected support (e.g., a partner, notes, rehearsal time).
Name math terms as depicted on flash cards.
State the steps needed to solve a visually depicted math problem using manipulatives.
Explain the steps used to solve a visually supported math problem.
Analyze the process for solving grade-level math problems with a partner.
Offer an alternative solution to solving a math problem with a small group.
Name the components of the Milky Way using visuals as a guide.
Restate the interconnectedness of the components of the Milky Way using visuals and notes/ graphic organizers.
Ask questions about the interconnectedness of the components of the Milky Way using visuals and notes/graphic organizers.
Analyze orally the interconnectedness of the components of the Milky Way using notes/graphic organizers in a small group.
Analyze orally the interconnectedness of the components of the Milky Way in a small group
Name historical figures or events in photographs and illustrations with a partner.
Answer WH-questions about historical figures or events from photographs, illustrations or videos in a small group.
Role-play scenes from the lives of historical figures or events with a team.
Engage in a classroom discussion about historical figures or events based on previously completed graphic organizer.
Debate or defend a decision or action of an historical figure or event in teams.
Make “To do” lists (pictures and words) using a picture dictionary.
Compose short phrases or sentences about personally relevant tasks (shopping, dining, personal hygiene) with a partner using sentence frames.
Construct simple paragraphs about personally relevant tasks using a graphic organizer.
Revise paragraphs about personally relevant tasks with a partner.
Write responses including figurative language about personally relevant tasks using study guides.
Label events in a story with sequence words (e.g., first, second, then, last) using an illustrated narrative or informational text.
Write phrases to demonstrate sequence from an illustrated narrative or informational text sentence frames (e.g., After that …; Finally…).
Compose sentences that convey sequence using a sequencing chart.
Construct a paragraph that uses some technical language (e.g., initially, finally) to convey sequence using model papers.
Edit multiple organized paragraphs that use technical language to sequence events using a rubric.
Label a bar graph with title, appropriate scale, labels and a key using a model.
Write phrases to describe patterns of data in charts and graphs using a visual example.
Compare and contrast data in charts and graphs using a Venn diagram.
Create an appropriate chart or graph for a given set of data while working with a partner.
Justify the process for solving a grade-level open-ended item dealing with data (e.g., why a circle graph would be the best way to report the data) using class notes.
Label a drawing/model of a plant cell using pre-printed word cards with a partner.
Label a drawing/model of a plant cell using a word bank from an illustrated model.
List the steps of photosynthesis in plants using a pictorial representation.
Produce a written paragraph explaining the steps of photosynthesis referencing information in a text.
Write a multiparagraph report explaining the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy on Earth.
Label pictures of historical events with a partner.
Write phrases or short sentences about visually supported historical events using sentence frames.
Compare and/or contrast visually supported historical events using a Venn diagram.
Generate an informative comparative summary of historical events with a writing frame in a small group.
Write an informative comparative essay about an historical event using primary sources with a rubric.

units.title: English language learners communicate information, ideas, and concepts necessary for academic success in the content area of SOCIAL STUDIES

outcomes.text: Level 1 Entering: Indicate where natural resources exist (e.g., Find an oil rig) from visually supported oral description.
Level 2 Beginning: Identify distribution of natural resources around the world (e.g., point to sites of solar energy on a map or globe) from visually supported oral description.
Level 3 Developing: Compare availability of natural resources between two or more countries from visually supported oral description.
Level 4 Expanding: Analyze distribution of products from natural resources among global markets from visually supported oral description.
Level 5 Bridging: Interpret implications of distribution of products from natural resources among global markets from visually supported oral description.
Level 1 Entering: Identify key vocabulary related to local, state and national government supported visually in L1 or L2
Level 2 Beginning: Locate the roles of local, state and national governments using a graphic organizer in a small group.
Level 3 Developing: Note the roles and responsibilities of local, state and national government using a Venn diagram with a partner.
Level 4 Expanding: Differentiate the roles of local, state and national governments using a Venn diagram.
Level 5 Bridging: Differentiate the responsibilities of local, state and national governments based on implicit and explicit texts with a partner.
Level 1 Entering: Respond to Yes/No questions about current or past events in world history with visual supports (e.g., photographs)..
Level 2 Beginning: Answer short answer questions about current or past events in world history using sentence starters and visual support.
Level 3 Developing: Discuss personal connections to current or past people or events in world history (e.g., I visited Tiananmen Square) using realia or visual supports.
Level 4 Expanding: Analyze current or past events in world history with a small group.
Level 5 Bridging: Critique current or past issues or policies in world history with a partner.
Level 1 Entering: Match key vocabulary with the physical characteristics of places on a map or a chart with a small group.
Level 2 Beginning: Label the physical characteristics of places with short descriptive phrases noted in a graphic organizer.
Level 3 Developing: Summarize the physical characteristics of places from information presented in a graphic organizer.
Level 4 Expanding: Create a multi- paragraph essay from an outline describing the physical characteristics of places or regions with a
Level 5 Bridging: Write a research paper analyzing the physical characteristics of places or regions using a graphic organizer.

units.title: English language learners communicate information, ideas, and concepts necessary for academic success in the content area of MATHEMATICS

outcomes.text: Level 1 Entering: Match math vocabulary to geometric figures in a small group.
Level 2 Emerging: Follow teacher directions to create a geometric figure using manipulatives.
Level 3 Developing: Identify geometric figures based on oral descriptions with a partner.
Level 4 Expanding: Create geometric figures based on multi- step oral directions with a partner.
Level 5 Bridging: Transform geometric shapes based on oral directions using computer software or other supports.
Level 1 Entering: Match data to the correct graph (e.g., data table to a circle graph) with a partner.
Level 2 Emerging: Organize data on a basic chart with a partner or a group.
Level 3 Developing: Interpret data in a graph working with a partner or a group.
Level 4 Expanding: Analyze conclusions drawn from data on a graph with a partner or a group.
Level 5 Bridging: Predict trends from data on a graph working with a partner or a group.
Level 1 Entering: Repeat the steps in the order of operations using a guided model with a partner.
Level 2 Emerging: Identify steps in the order of operations with a small group.
Level 3 Developing: Sequence the steps to solve a problem involving the order of operations with a small group. (e.g., add before you subtract in an algebraic equation).
Level 4 Expanding: Explain the solution to a problem involving the order of operations using visual supports.
Level 5 Bridging: Analyze the solution to a problem involving the order of operations with a partner.
Level 1 Entering: Label symbols found in algebraic equations, inequalities or expressions.
Level 2 Emerging: Illustrate the steps used to sequence or solve an algebraic equation, inequality or expression with a partner and/or small group.
Level 3 Developing: Compose a simple algebraic equation, inequality or expression using a guided model.
Level 4 Expanding: Write a word problem that fits an algebraic equation, inequality or expression with a partner.
Level 5 Bridging: Justify the solution of an algebraic equation, inequality or expression using figures, notations and complex sentences.

units.title: English language learners communicate information, ideas, and concepts necessary for academic success in the content area of LANGUAGE ARTS

outcomes.text: Level 1 Entering: Match oral content vocabulary to visuals with a small group.
Level 2 Emerging: Match oral phrases and statements to media, objects, or illustrations with a partner.
Level 3 Developing: Sort or sequence events from oral commentary with visual support and graphic organizers.
Level 4 Expanding: Identify cause and effect from oral discourse (e.g., watch a video clip and predict a character’s response) with a partner
Level 5 Bridging: Identify personal connections from oral descriptions of a character’s actions and/or experiences using a graphic organizer.
Level 1 Entering: Match a person to his/her acts or accomplishments using visuals.
Level 2 Emerging: Sequence the events of a person’s life using a timeline.
Level 3 Developing: Identify motivational factors in a person’s life using visuals and annotated text.
Level 4 Expanding: Interpret the impact of a person’s life on others or society from visually supported text (e.g., How did Rosa Park’s decisions affect the Civil Rights movement?)
Level 5 Bridging: Analyze a person’s life choices using grade level text (e.g., was a decision. beneficial or harmful).
Level 1 Entering: Ask and answer WH- questions about text features using visually guided prompts with a small group of students.
Level 2 Emerging: Ask and answer text features using pictures, graphs, or charts with a partner.
Level 3 Developing: Ask and answer context features of text using graphic organizers.
Level 4 Expanding: Discuss the key details and events of a grade- level non-fiction text in a small group using class notes.
Level 5 Bridging: Discuss the key details and events of a grade- level non-fiction text using class notes
Level 1 Entering: Produce key words or phrases on a relevant topic using bilingual or picture dictionaries.
Level 2 Emerging: Produce phrases/short sentences using various writing styles with a guided model.
Level 3 Developing: Produce paragraphs in various genres from notes with a guided model.
Level 4 Expanding: Edit and revise rough drafts across various genres using checklists or rubrics with a partner.
Level 5 Bridging: Produce grade-level writing across various genres using rubrics and electronic writing tools.

units.title: English language learners communicate in English for SOCIAL AND INSTRUCTIONAL purposes within the school setting

outcomes.text: Level 1 Entering: Follow one-step oral directions from teacher supported by gestures.
Level 2 Emerging: Sequence events with visual support (i.e., Follow a daily schedule).
Level 3 Developing: Follow multi-step oral directions to select materials or resources needed to complete tasks with a partner.
Level 4 Expanding: Follow-up, process and respond to announcements over the intercom with peer support.
Level 5 Bridging: Analyze and interpret the appropriateness of oral messages or information from a variety of sources (such as: popular songs and voicemail messages) with a small group.
Level 1 Entering: Sort information from multiple visually supported sources with a partner.
Level 2 Emerging: Identify important information (e.g., by highlighting) from multiple visually supported sources support with a partner
Level 3 Developing: Categorize (e.g., best, maybe, unlikely) options from multiple sources with a graphic organizers
Level 4 Expanding: Summarize information from a variety of visually supported print resources.
Level 5 Bridging: Evaluate hypotheses based on information from a visually supported text.
Level 1 Entering: Answer yes/no questions about types of music, games, TV programs or recreational with visual support.
Level 2 Emerging: Ask WH questions about preferred movies, magazines, stories, or authors with a partner.
Level 3 Developing: Recommend games, songs, books, films or computer programs with a partner.
Level 4 Expanding: Compare and contrast plays, films, books, songs, computer programs or magazine articles using realia.
Level 5 Bridging: In a multimedia presentation, critique and evaluate plays, films, books, songs, computer programs, or magazine articles with a small group.

Level 1 Entering: Match pictures of water to its various states using visual cues.
Level 2 Emerging: Categorize water according to its states and properties with a partner.
Level 3 Developing: Predict how the state of water will change given various real-world scenarios in videos.
Level 4 Expanding: Compare and contrast the unique properties of water to other liquids with a graphic organizer and teacher direction.
Level 5 Bridging: Reflect on how human influence impacts the state of water with a small group.
Select traits related to patterns of inheritance (e.g., blond vs. black hair, short tails vs. long tails) with visual support.
Identify the different parts of a DNA molecule on a diagram with a partner.
Describe the role of protein synthesis in cell reproduction using poster support.
Analyze genetic mutations and the how the DNA sequence may or may not affect phenotype using illustrations/photographs.
Draw conclusions about the impact of breeding using guided notes (e.g., dog, fruit, flower breeding).
Name examples of extinct and non-extinct species using flash cards (e.g., t-rex, wooly mammoth, raccoons).
Identify and describe artifacts that support the theory of evolution (e.g., Identify pictures of fossil skeletons).
Describe the possible causes of species extinction using online video resources.
Discuss how natural selection can impact a population in a small group.
Debate various theories of evolution, creation, and extinction of life with teacher modeling and class notes.
Label a simple diagram of the food chain using graphic support.
Take notes on a graphic organizer to show predator/prey relationships using phrase wall support.
Write an outline describing a food web which includes producers, consumers, and decomposers with template support (e.g., descriptors of the roles of each organism).
Summarize the flow of energy within an ecosystem with the support of a model (i.e., as it relates to the food web).
Produce a research report explaining how the flow of energy within an ecosystem changes when one element is removed with partner support (i.e., as it relates to the food web).
